Abstract
Objective. To quantify spatial population structure, gene flow and candidate signatures of local selection in 
Plasmodium falciparum across Ghana's agro-ecological zones using the MalariaGEN Pf8 release; to measure 
the zone-level frequencies of the canonical antimalarial resistance codons, and the haplotypes they form 
within isolates; and to establish whether zone-level differentiation is detectable at all before any locus-
specific signal is interpreted.
Design limits, stated first. Zone is not an isolable variable in this dataset. Three of the four represented zones 
are each filled by exactly one administrative region (Guinea savanna / Upper East, coastal savanna / Greater 
Accra, transitional zone / Brong Ahafo); collection year differs systematically between zones; and four of the 
six zone pairs share no Pf8 sequencing study at all, including coastal savanna versus Guinea savanna, the pair 
that carries every headline number. Ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing batch 
are collinear by construction. Every zone-level result below is a statement about that compound variable. It is 
arranged broadly from south to north, but not monotonically: the transitional zone is the second-most-
northern of the four and is represented by only 25 analysed isolates, and it breaks the south-to-north 
ordering in all but one of the variables examined here - the single exception is pfaat1 S258L, which declines 
monotonically from coastal savanna through deciduous forest and the transitional zone to Guinea savanna - 
so no claim of a latitudinal cline is made from the four zone means alone. No adjustment within these data 
can decompose the compound variable.
Data. Pf8 contains 33,325 samples and 12,493,205 variant sites. Ghana contributes 6,653 samples, of which 
4,905 pass the release's own quality control. Isolates were collected between 2009 and 2021 and are 
geolocated only to administrative level 1, giving seven distinct coordinates across seven regions. A spatial join 
to a Ghana agro-ecological zone layer placed these 4,905 in four zones: Guinea savanna (n = 3,605), 
deciduous forest (n = 815), coastal savanna (n = 435) and transitional zone (n = 50); the smaller zone counts 
quoted under Methods are for the 1,900 isolates that survive this analysis's own sample QC. The Sudan 
savanna and the wet-evergreen and moist-evergreen forest zones are unrepresented. The zone layer itself 
has no citable published source: it is an unattributed re-host of an anonymous ArcGIS Online item, identified 
byte-for-byte by checksum, and is used here as accessed rather than as authoritative.
Methods. Genotypes were obtained from the Pf8 Zarr store over HTTPS, restricted to Ghanaian samples, 
sites passing the release filter, biallelic single-nucleotide polymorphisms only (the ingest mask is FILTER_PASS 
& is_snp & numalt == 1), and the GT, AD, DP and GQ fields. Sample quality control applied a within-host fixation 
index (Fws) threshold of 0.95, a call-rate floor of 0.80, a heterozygosity outlier rule and clonal pruning; mixed 
calls were resolved to the majority allele by read depth and allele counts taken as one allele per isolate. 
Variant missingness is now recomputed after the sample cut rather than before it, which yields 3,916 SNPs 
across 1,900 isolates (mean missingness 2.95%): Guinea savanna 1,334, deciduous forest 337, coastal 
savanna 204, transitional zone 25. Analyses comprised three ordinations of the published Pf8 genotype-
distance matrix (originally computed on the 4,905 release-QC-pass isolates and now re-run on the 1,900-
isolate analysis set, by re-slicing the distance submatrix rather than reusing the cached full-set one), pairwise 
Hudson FST with a block jackknife, ADMIXTURE at K = 1-8 with cross-validation, Mantel tests of isolation by 
distance at zone and region level with a leave-one-population-out jackknife, TreeMix with 0-5 migration 
edges and jackknife edge standard errors, and a BayPass XtX scan calibrated against 100,000 pseudo-
observed neutral SNPs with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values. Two further checks were added at final revision 
and both are reported below: a six-scenario threshold sensitivity analysis that rebuilds the analysis matrix

Principal findings: population structure. Zone differentiation is very low, and after the sensitivity analysis this 
is the best-supported finding in the report. The largest pairwise FST is 0.00232 (SE 0.00053, 95% CI 0.00128-
0.00336) between coastal and Guinea savanna, and one of six pairs - Guinea savanna versus the transitional 
zone (n = 25) - has a confidence interval spanning zero; the other five have strictly positive lower bounds. 
Varying the two thresholds that define the dataset leaves the maximum pairwise FST within 0.00204-0.00255 
across all six scenarios, over sample sizes from 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and SNP counts from 3,275 to 10,876. 
Two directions within that range are worth recording: relaxing the Fws cut slightly raises FST (0.00232 to 
0.00255 with no Fws filter at all), so polyclonal isolates were not masking differentiation, and tripling the SNP 
count at MAF >= 0.01 lowers it (0.00204), as expected if rarer variants are less differentiated between zones. 
Isolation by distance, by contrast, is not a robust result. At administrative-region level the test is significant 
at the published thresholds (Mantel r = 0.427, p = 0.025 with negative FST pairs floored to zero; r = 0.414, p = 
0.041 without flooring the three negative pairs) and it is absent at zone level (r = 0.471, p = 0.122, significant 
in 0 of 4 leave-one-zone-out replicates, and with four populations admitting only 24 distinct label 
permutations). But across the six threshold scenarios the region-level test is significant in only two: the 
published thresholds and MAF >= 0.02 (r = 0.434, p = 0.047 censored, p = 0.050 uncensored, so that scenario 
is marginal in both directions). It fails at every relaxation of the Fws monoclonality cut (Fws >= 0.90, r = 0.318, p 
= 0.087; Fws >= 0.80, r = 0.256, p = 0.169; no Fws filter, r = 0.245, p = 0.179) and at MAF >= 0.01 (r = 0.432, p = 
0.062). It is also significant in only four of seven leave-one-region-out replicates, collapsing when Upper East 
is dropped. The finding holds at the published thresholds and almost nowhere else, and is reported here as 
not robust - not as a supported result, and not as a weak but real distance effect. ADMIXTURE cross-
validation error is minimised at K = 2 (0.83925) over K = 1 (0.84384), an improvement of 0.00459 on a near-
flat curve. The K = 2 minor component is not uniform across zones (means 0.092 deciduous forest, 0.085 
coastal savanna, 0.053 Guinea savanna, 0.042 transitional zone; Kruskal-Wallis H = 105.4, p = 1.1 x 10 to the 
-22). That is a real contrast - coastal and forest high, Guinea savanna and transitional low - concordant with 
the FST ranking but not a monotone latitudinal cline, and of negligible magnitude. TreeMix, now run with edge 
standard errors, selects a descriptive graph with two migration edges — a model choice, not a count of 
historical migration events (weights 0.152, p = 7.5 x 10 to the -4, and 0.805, p = 3.3 x 10 to the -16; variance 
explained 0.9969 at m = 2 against 0.8970 at m = 0); a third edge is indistinguishable from zero (p = 0.33). The 
edge tests are conditional on a topology, root and edge count all fixed beforehand, and the variance-
explained criterion across the full m = 0 to 5 sweep still prefers m = 3, so the two criteria disagree and are 
reconciled here on identifiability grounds.

1. Introduction and background
1.1 The problem
Malaria transmission in Ghana is spatially heterogeneous, and the heterogeneity tracks ecology. The country 
spans a south-to-north gradient of agro-ecological zones that differ in rainfall, vector species composition, 
seasonality and consequently in entomological inoculation rate. If parasite populations in these zones are 
demographically separate to any meaningful degree, then drug-resistance alleles, antigenic variants and 
locally adaptive alleles can differ in frequency between them. If instead the zones exchange parasites freely, 
an allele arising anywhere will spread everywhere, and the surveillance question becomes one of timing 
rather than of geography.
The two scenarios demand different control responses and are distinguishable from genomic data. The 
present analysis addresses the prior question that both depend on: how much spatial structure is there in 
Ghanaian P. falciparum, and is it enough to support zone-level inference at all?
[Interpreted] A refinement of the framing. An earlier version of this report ran the argument directly from the 
amount of neutral structure to a conclusion about surveillance design - that if the parasites form one 
population, spatially sparse sentinel sampling is representative. That step does not hold, and the project's 
own literature review argues against it: selection builds connectivity and locus-specific allele trajectories that 
neutral demography does not predict, so a resistance allele can have a site-specific frequency even under 
neutral panmixia. Neutral differentiation and marker-frequency representativeness are two distinct 
quantities and have to be measured separately. This analysis therefore does both - genome-wide 
differentiation at common variants, and direct resistance-marker frequencies by zone - and reports them as 
two findings rather than deriving the second from the first.

signatures of selection.docx", 145 paragraphs, approximately 11,400 words) set out the biological rationale, 
the resistance-marker panel and the published context. This report does not restate that material. It 
documents what was computed, on what data, with which decisions, and what the output actually shows,

1.2 Objectives addressed by the present analysis

• Administrative region. Three of the four zones are each filled by exactly one region - Guinea savanna by 
Upper East (3,605 of 3,605 release-QC-pass isolates), coastal savanna by Greater Accra (435 of 435), 
transitional zone by Brong Ahafo (50 of 50); only deciduous forest draws on more than one (Ashanti, 
Central, Eastern, Volta). For those three, "zone" and "region" are the same variable, and any difference 
attributed to ecology could equally be attributed to the region's health system, drug supply, sampling 
protocol or collection year.
• Collection period. Zone-level year distributions differ systematically: Guinea savanna spans 2009-2019 
with a 2018 peak, coastal savanna is concentrated in 2016-2018, deciduous forest in 2013-2021, and the 
transitional zone falls entirely in 2011-2013. Over 2009-2021 Ghana changed first-line therapy and 
scaled up chemoprevention, so drug-related allele frequencies would be expected to move with time 
independently of geography. The confounding is not removable by reweighting, because for the 
transitional zone and the coastal savanna the year ranges do not overlap at all. The same fact makes 
every resistance frequency in this report a 2009-2021 average rather than a current value, including the 
pfk13 zeros.
• Sequencing study (new in this version). Pf8 isolates arrive through named partner studies, and in Ghana 
those studies are almost perfectly nested within zones. Four of the six zone pairs share no study 
whatsoever - coastal savanna versus Guinea savanna, coastal savanna versus transitional, deciduous 
forest versus Guinea savanna, and deciduous forest versus transitional - and the first of these is the pair 
behind the maximum FST and the polyclonality contrast. Each zone is dominated by one study: the 
transitional zone is 100% one study (1083-PF-GH-CONWAY, 50 of 50), coastal savanna 89% (387 of 435, 
1241-PF-GH-ANINAGYEI), Guinea savanna 74% (2,678 of 3,605, 1168-PF-GH-AMENGA-ETEGO-SM) and 
deciduous forest 48% (391 of 815, 1200-PF-GH-MAIGA-SM). Study-associated heterogeneity in this 
dataset is demonstrable, not hypothetical: holding zone constant, so that study varies together with 
collection year, finer geography and recruitment, call rate differs between the six studies within Guinea 
savanna at p = 2.8 x 10 to the -197. Deciduous forest draws on five studies in all; across the four of them 
large enough to test (811 of the zone's 815 isolates, the fifth contributing only 4) call rate differs at p = 
7.7 x 10 to the -88, and the polyclonal fraction ranges from 0.430 to 0.578 (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0019).
• Spatial resolution. Isolates are geolocated only to administrative level 1, so 1,900 isolates carry seven 
distinct coordinates between them. No sub-regional analysis is possible, and isolation by distance rests 
on 21 pairs derived from 7 points - a test fragile enough that, as the threshold sensitivity analysis shows, 
it changes verdict when either of the two dataset-defining cuts is moved.

1.3 Research questions as operationalised
The thesis questions were translated into the following testable forms. The translation is itself an analytical 
decision and is revisited in Section 5.
1. Is between-zone differentiation distinguishable from zero? Operationalised as pairwise Hudson FST with 
block-jackknife confidence intervals, and - new in this version - recomputed under six scenarios that vary 
the Fws and MAF thresholds, so that the magnitude is reported with its sensitivity to the cuts that define 
the dataset rather than at one setting only.
2. Does genetic distance increase with geographic distance? Operationalised as a Mantel test of FST/(1 - FST) 
against log geographic distance, run at both zone and region level, with the permutation test seeded, 
the censoring of negative FST pairs disclosed and reported both ways, a leave-one-population-out 
jackknife to test whether any single population carries the result, and - new in this version - 
recomputation of the region-level test under all six threshold scenarios, since a permutation test on 21 
pairs from 7 points can depend heavily on the matrix it is given. This question is the one whose answer 
changed at final revision.
3. Do individual isolates assign to zone-associated ancestry components? Operationalised as ADMIXTURE 
at K = 1-8 with 10-fold cross-validation, visual inspection of three ordinations - now computed on the 
1,900-isolate analysis set as well as on the 4,905 pre-QC isolates the published figures used, by re-slicing 
the distance submatrix - and an explicit Kruskal-Wallis test of the minor-component proportion against 
zone, so that the magnitude and the significance of any zone effect are reported separately.
4. Is there evidence of gene flow beyond a simple bifurcating population tree? Operationalised as TreeMix 
with 0-5 migration edges, run with jackknife standard errors so that each edge carries a p-value and the 
number of edges is informed by a test rather than only by the shape of the likelihood curve.
5. Which loci are more differentiated than neutral demography predicts? Operationalised as a BayPass XtX 
scan with a threshold calibrated on pseudo-observed data simulated under the estimated population 
covariance matrix, reported alongside the expected number of false positives at that threshold, the 
implied expected-null-exceedance ratio, per-SNP Benjamini-Hochberg q-values, and - new in this version 
- a per-SNP call-quality audit of every outlier against the rest of the scanned panel, so that a high XtX 
value is reported with the quality evidence for or against the call behind it.
6. New, and now rebuilt. What are the zone-level frequencies of the canonical antimalarial resistance 
residues, and of the haplotypes they form within isolates? Operationalised not by annotation matching

spectrum including the reference residue is reported with Wilson confidence intervals and a four-zone

[Interpreted] The practical reading is as follows. Study confounding does not threaten the central finding that

3. Methodology
The analysis is driven by scripts/run_all.sh. It comprises the nine numbered stages of the supplied pipeline, 
plus Stage 3a, written during this session to replace a failed VCF download, and Stage 3b, the supplied per-
isolate quality-control script that run_all.sh labels as part of Stage 3 but that is given its own row in Table 3.1, 
and four stages added after review: Stage 10, a multiallelic-aware resistance marker panel; Stage 11, a 
diagnostic for the confounding of agro-ecological zone with sequencing study; Stage 12, which replaces Stage 
10's marker panel entirely after an external critique showed that Stage 10's method of identifying markers — 
matching SnpEff protein-change strings against a hand-written list — could not see a resistance allele that is 
the reference residue and could not see a residue requiring two changes in one codon (both failures 
occurred); and Stage 13, which rebuilds the analysis matrix under six settings of the two thresholds that 
define the dataset and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test under each. Stage 13 is the 
stage whose result matters most, and it does not go the manuscript's way: it leaves near-panmixia stronger 
than before and it removes the support for isolation by distance, which is significant at the published 
thresholds and at almost none of the others. That is a loss of a result, not a refinement of one, and Section 
3.14 states it as such. Stage 10 is retained in the repository and in Table 3.1 for the record, but no number in 
this manuscript now comes from it; Section 3.10 sets out the replacement method and Section 3.10.1 the 
reason it was needed. Stages run in order; each writes its outputs to disk so that a failure costs one stage 
rather than the whole run. That caching is stated here with its qualification rather than as a design virtue, 
because it was also the pipeline's most dangerous defect: the guards skipped a stage whenever its output file 
already existed, without checking whether the input had changed, so when the SNP panel moved from 3,359 
to 3,916 SNPs, ADMIXTURE and TreeMix silently reported the previous day's results as "stage finished". Only 
Stage 8 carried an assertion that caught it. The guards now require the output to be newer than its input; 
Section 3.13 sets out what happened and what was changed. Stages 10 to 13 are read-only with respect to 
everything upstream: they create new output files and modify none, so no estimate in Sections 6.1 to 6.7 
depends on them. Two further checks changed no stage's method but changed what the existing stages 
describe: Stage 3's three ordinations were re-run on the 1,900-isolate analysis set rather than the 4,905 pre-
QC isolates (Section 3.4.1), and the 19 XtX outliers were audited against the Pf8 per-variant quality 
annotations (Section 3.11.1). This section describes each stage: what it does, why, what it assumes, and how 
it constrains what follows. Where a method changed in the corrected re-run, or in the rebuild that followed 
the external critique, or in these final checks, the change and its motivation are stated in place rather than 
relegated to a revision log.

gives the ceiling any embedding could achieve.

3.6 Stage 3b — isolate quality control
Four per-isolate checks are applied, computed from a panel of 50,000 biallelic PASS SNPs spread 
proportionally across all 14 contigs.
Within-host fixation index (Fws). Fws measures how far an isolate's read-level allele frequencies depart from 
the population's. A clonal infection has read frequencies near 0 or 1 at every site and Fws near 1; a mixed 
infection carries intermediate frequencies and a lower value. It is computed as Fws = 1 − (Σ Hw,i / Σ Hs,i), 
where Hw = 2q(1 − q) from the isolate's own read counts and Hs = 2p(1 − p) from pooled read counts across 
qualifying isolates. Sites contribute only where total depth is at least 5. The conventional monoclonality 
threshold of 0.95 is applied (config.py MIN_FWS = 0.95). That threshold is a convention and not a property of 
these data, it discards the majority of the isolates, and Section 3.14 reports what the results do when it is 
relaxed.

Call rate. The proportion of panel SNPs with a genotype call. The pipeline applies an absolute floor and, 
optionally, a median-absolute-deviation outlier rule; the choice between them is discussed in Section 5.4.
Heterozygosity outliers. Blood-stage P. falciparum is haploid, so a heterozygous call indicates a mixed 
infection or a genotyping error rather than true heterozygosity. Isolates more than three median absolute 
deviations above the median heterozygous call rate are flagged. This check is largely redundant with Fws and 
is retained as an independent cross-check.
Clonal pruning. Near-identical isolates (outbreak-linked or repeat-sampled parasites) inflate within-zone 
homogeneity and therefore inflate between-zone FST. The cached Ghanaian distance submatrix from Stage 3 
is thresholded at CLONAL_THRESHOLD = 0.00005, connected components are extracted with a single-linkage 
rule, and one representative is retained per component — chosen by best call rate, then best Fws, then 
identifier, so the choice is deterministic.

3.10.2 The method: reconstruct the codon, report every residue
The script works at the codon rather than at the annotation string. Each requested codon is mapped to its 
three genomic positions through the gene's CDS, read from the same PlasmoDB-71 GFF the rest of the 
pipeline uses: CDS segments are concatenated in coordinate order, reversed for minus-strand genes so that 
the order is translation order, the total length is asserted to be a multiple of three, and codon i is positions 
3i−2 to 3i of that sequence. The reference bases at those three positions are read from the 3D7 reference 
genome FASTA, reverse-complemented on the minus strand, and translated, so the reference residue is read 
from the genome rather than assumed from the marker's name. Every variant record in the Pf8 Zarr at any 
of the three positions is then collected — regardless of numalt and regardless of is_snp — each isolate's 
called alleles are substituted into the reference codon, and the result is translated. The output is the full 
residue spectrum at each codon, the reference residue included and labelled as such, so a resistance allele 
cannot hide in the reference and a residue requiring two substitutions cannot be missed.

departure from the Stage 4a and Stage 10 rule, which resolves a mixed call to the allele with more reads

each position independently by read depth can manufacture a residue that no single parasite in the infection 
carries. The cost is a per-codon denominator slightly below 1,900, and the benefit is that no reported residue

3.10.4 Frequencies, intervals and tests
Point estimates. The frequency of a residue is computed per codon, as the count of isolates carrying it 
divided by the count of isolates with a non-missing reconstructed codon there, within the 1,900-isolate 
analysis set. Denominators therefore differ between codons and between zones, and are reported per cell. 
Because the spectrum is complete, the frequencies at a codon sum to one; the reference residue's frequency 
is reported on the same footing as any other, which is what makes pfdhps G437 at 0.897 visible at all.
Wilson score intervals. Confidence intervals are Wilson score intervals rather than Wald intervals. This is not 
a cosmetic choice. Many codons sit at or very near 1.000 — 33 of the 57 are fixed at the reference residue in 
every called isolate — and the Transitional zone contributes 25 isolates. A Wald interval at p-hat = 0 or 1 has 
zero width, and at small n it can extend outside [0, 1]; the Wilson interval is well behaved in both cases and 
has better coverage at the extremes, which is where this panel's most consequential readings sit. It is what 
lets a zero be reported as a bounded negative: pfdhfr IRNL at 0.000 carries the interval 0.000 to 0.002 over 
1,874 complete cases, and the Transitional zone's own zero carries 0.000 to 0.133 over 25.

count table for that residue. The test is of heterogeneity, not of a north-south trend: a significant result says 
the four zones differ, and the direction of any cline must be read from the frequencies themselves — the 
more so because the Transitional zone is the second-most-northern of the four, so a frequency ordering is 
not a geographic ordering. The test family is residues rather than codons, as the first sentence implies:

3.11 False-discovery accounting in the XtX scan
The problem. A quantile threshold is not a significance test. Calling a SNP an outlier when its XtX exceeds the 
0.999 quantile of the pseudo-observed null guarantees that 0.1 per cent of strictly neutral SNPs will be called, 
by construction, however neutral the genome is. The original Stage 8 reported a threshold and a count of 
SNPs above it, with no statement of how many were expected under the null — so the outlier list had no 
error rate attached, and the reader had no way to judge how much of it to believe.
What the step now reports. step08c_calibrate_xtx.py was extended to report four things alongside the 
threshold.
12. Expected false positives at the threshold. The quantile and the panel size give this immediately: at 
the 0.999 quantile over 3,916 SNPs, 3.9 are expected above threshold under the null.
13. An expected-null-exceedance ratio at the threshold — expected false positives under the assumed 
null divided by the number of SNPs actually called. It is an expectation under that null, not a measured 
false-discovery fraction. With 19 SNPs above a threshold of XtX 10.840 and 3.9 expected, that is 20.6 
per cent.
14. Per-SNP p-values against the pseudo-observed null. Each observed XtX is ranked within the sorted 
pseudo-observed distribution and assigned p = (n_pod − rank + 1) / (n_pod + 1), which is a Monte Carlo 
one-sided tail probability under that fitted null and is bounded below by 1/(n_pod + 1) rather than being 
reported as zero.
15. Benjamini–Hochberg q-values, computed over all 3,916 SNPs by the standard step-up procedure 
with monotonicity enforced (step08c_calibrate_xtx.py:114, with the write at :139). The q-values are the 
values in Table 3.3, and logs/stage8.log:115-119 prints the counts at q ≤ 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2. The

5.7.1 The ingest filter on PASS biallelic SNPs: the first defect that changed a conclusion
Of the twenty-seven defects in Table 5.2, most changed a number, a standard error, a reproducibility 
property or a resource bound. Three changed a conclusion, and each is separated from the rest: the ingest 
filter described here, the annotation-string matching that forced a complete rebuild of the marker panel 
(Section 5.7.3), and the misreading of the pfaat1 functional work (Table 5.2, Pass 4, and the note at the end 
of this subsection).
[Observed] step03a_fetch_callset_zarr.py builds the genome-wide callset under FILTER_PASS & is_snp & numalt == 1. 
Read as English, that is "PASS, SNP, biallelic" — a filter so conventional that it was proposed, accepted and 
implemented without comment (Section 5.1). In Pf8, however, most canonical antimalarial-resistance codons 
are either multiallelic or carry a spanning-deletion ALT allele, so the mask excluded them, and the two tests 
do not contribute equally: pfcrt K76T and M74I, pfmdr1 N86Y and pfdhps A581G all fail is_snp outright, while 
pfdhps K540E passes is_snp and is excluded by numalt == 2. Across the nine panel genes, 13,367 PASS records 
enter the filter and 3,330 leave it: 10,037 are dropped, including 28 of the 44 canonical codon-allele records 
on the list then in use. That list has since been replaced twice (Section 5.7.3); the filter's effect on the genes' 
records is a property of the filter and does not depend on it.

as biology. The abstract and §6.8 both reported that no validated antimalarial resistance locus appears

6.9.2 Method: reconstruct the codon, report the whole spectrum
[Observed] scripts/step12_codon_panel.py discards annotation matching. For each requested codon it maps the 
codon to its three genomic positions through the gene's CDS, collects every variant record at those positions 
regardless of numalt, is_snp or ALT type, applies each isolate's alleles to the reference codon, and translates 
the result. The output is the full residue spectrum at each codon, including the reference residue, so a 
resistance allele cannot hide in the reference and a two-SNP residue cannot be missed. Genotypes are 
collapsed by the same majority-allele ploidy rule used in Step 4a; a codon in which an isolate's calls are mixed 
is recorded as uncalled for that isolate rather than being assigned a residue. Frequencies are reported per 
agro-ecological zone with Wilson 95 per cent confidence intervals, and heterogeneity across the four zones is 
tested by χ² on residue counts. The same 1,900 isolates are used as in every other analysis in this chapter.

rather than independence: the FST summary has been recomputed under six combinations of the two 
thresholds that define the dataset, and the maximum pairwise value moves only between 0.00204 and

hypothesis — "is not supported" — concluding instead that chloroquine was "the primary selective force". 
Framing the Ghanaian cline as amodiaquine-maintained therefore did not extend the paper's finding; it 
contradicted it.
[Interpreted] And the effect itself is modest and conditional. S258L raised chloroquine IC50 1.5-fold, in a 
single chloroquine-resistant Southeast Asian line (NHP4026), with epistasis between S258L and F313S and 
an explicit caveat that the effect depends on pfcrt background. The much-cited rise from 0 per cent to 97 per 
cent is Gambian, 1984–2014; the paper says nothing about Ghana. The accurate description is therefore: 
pfaat1 S258L is a variant with a demonstrated but modest, epistasis- and background-dependent effect that 
potentiates chloroquine resistance — not a validated resistance determinant, and not a marker of any current  
drug. One detail of this sample sharpens the caveat: pfaat1 F313S, the epistatic partner, is absent — codon 
313 is at the reference residue in all 1,900 isolates — so the interaction the experiment demonstrated cannot 
be operating in these parasites at all.
[Hypothesized] What might maintain the cline, with the candidates ranked by how well they are supported. 
Three non-exclusive possibilities, and the honest ordering is not the previous draft's. (i) Historical 
persistence. Chloroquine was first-line therapy in Ghana until 2005 and the paper's own conclusion is that 
chloroquine was the selective force; a chloroquine-era allele decaying unevenly is the explanation most 
consistent with the source. (ii) A documented fitness cost without drug, which would slow reversion rather 
than reverse it and is the reason a standing intermediate frequency is expected rather than either fixation or 
zero. (iii) Residual 4-aminoquinoline pressure from artesunate–amodiaquine, a current first-line ACT whose 
deployment is not uniform across the country. This third possibility is offered as an untested possible 
contemporary driver only. Nothing in these data tests it, no drug-pressure or deployment data were available 
to this analysis, and the experimental work that does exist found amodiaquine shifts below the clinical 
threshold and argued against the partner-drug hypothesis. It is a hypothesis worth stating and not a reading 
of the evidence.

AQ deployment and adherence rather than with any ecological variable, and should be unstable over time as 
treatment policy changes. Neither prediction is tested here, and the alternative that S258L tracks some

[Interpreted] What the pattern of these checks says about the verification, stated once. This is the fourth 
consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect. The pattern is consistent across all four: 
each layer was checked for internal consistency against this project's own outputs, and what escaped was 
external correctness — whether the marker list matched an authoritative source, whether the annotation 
direction matched the reference genome, whether a co-occurrence claim had co-occurrence data behind it. 
The verification architecture was built to catch stale numbers, and it did catch them. It was not built to ask 
whether the right question was being asked of the data. The four checks added in the previous revision — the 
panel rebuild by codon reconstruction, the per-sample comparison against MalariaGEN call by call, the 
within-isolate haplotype counts in place of marginals, and the check against the WHO compendium — are all 
external by construction, which is the point of them. The three added in this revision are of a third kind again, 
and worth distinguishing: they vary the analyst's own choices rather than compare against anything outside. 
That is what caught the isolation-by-distance result, and nothing else could have. No external reference 
would have flagged it, because the number was correctly computed at the thresholds the pipeline specifies; it 
was the choice of thresholds, not the arithmetic, that was carrying the result. A number can be right, 
reproducible and externally consistent, and the conclusion drawn from it still not survive the decision that 
produced it.

[Interpreted] A closing assessment. The analysis has done what a baseline characterisation should do: 
established the scale of structure, found it to be small, identified precisely which design features limit what 
can be inferred, and produced a short candidate list for follow-up. What has changed across the three rounds 
is the standing of the negative results, the standing of our own corrections, and now the standing of a 
positive result. The absence of resistance loci from the outlier scan was not a result at all but a filter artefact, 
and correcting it converted the thesis's third objective from a null finding into its best-supported positive one 
— pfdhps G437 at 0.897 and zone-structured, the pfdhfr triple mutant measured as a haplotype at 0.771, and 
pfaat1 S258L as a strong candidate whose demonstrated functional effect is modest and background-
dependent. The absence of artemisinin resistance is now genuinely tested, across the complete WHO-
validated and candidate sets, on 1,845 to 1,876 called isolates per codon over 2009–2021, and genuinely 
negative. But the first correction of the panel was itself wrong in four ways, and only an external reader 
caught it. The honest conclusion is therefore two claims rather than one. A negative result is worth nothing

until the thing it denies has been shown to be measurable. And internal consistency is not correctness: every 
defect in the first corrected panel came from a list, a direction or a label taken on trust, and the verification 
architecture built to catch stale numbers was never built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. The 
third round adds a third claim, and it is the least comfortable of the three. Four checks this list carried as 
outstanding were run, and the one previously described here as addressing "the two most likely reviewer 
objections" removed a finding instead of answering them: isolation by distance survives neither a relaxation 
of the monoclonality cut nor a lower MAF floor, and is significant at two of six threshold settings. The gain 
and the loss come from the same six runs. The check that destroyed the spatial finding is the check that made 
near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript, because FST moved by less than 0.0005 while 
the Mantel p-value crossed 0.05 four times. A result that holds only at the thresholds that produced it was 
never a result; it was a setting. The manuscript is shorter by one finding and better by one method, and the 
third claim is simply that: a threshold is a hypothesis, and until it has been varied, every conclusion 
downstream of it is conditional on a number nobody tested.

On pfcrt codon 75 — not a naming discrepancy. The previous version reported that Pf8's SnpEff annotation labels 
the ALT at pfcrt codon 75 as Asp while MalariaGEN calls it Glu, described this as the one marker-naming discrepancy 
among 23, and credited MalariaGEN with being right on the biology. The diagnosis was wrong. Codon 75 carries two 
variants — 403621 (A>G, annotated Asn75Asp) and 403623 (T>A, annotated Asn75Lys) — and Asn→Glu requires 
both, so no single-variant annotation can name N75E at all. The appearance of a discrepancy was created entirely by 
identifying markers from annotation strings. Reconstructed from the codon, residue 75 is Glu at 0.071 (n = 1,874), 
exactly matching the other CVIET component residues, and it agrees with MalariaGEN on every one of the 1,874 
jointly called isolates. There is no discrepancy to follow a convention about: there is one residue, Glu, and it is ours 
and MalariaGEN's alike.
